info.title: ScrapeUnblocker API
info.description: Public API for the ScrapeUnblocker proxy/anti-bot service. Authenticate every request with the `x-scrapeunblocker-key` header. Documented here: page-source extraction, Google SERP scraping, image fetch, and the dedicated plugin endpoints (search engines, marketplaces, reviews, travel, social and more). All other paths exist for internal operations and are intentionally hidden from this spec.

post.summary: Fetch the HTML (or parsed JSON) for any URL
post.description: Routes the URL through the appropriate anti-bot bypass chain (site-specific handlers, real-browser rendering, rotating proxies). Returns the prettified HTML by default; when the target answers with JSON, that JSON exactly as served. Set `markdown=true` to receive the page as clean Markdown (`text/markdown`) for LLMs and agents: by default only the main content, with absolute links (`main_content_only=false` keeps the whole page). Set `parsed_data=true` to receive a structured JSON payload extracted via Schema.org / __NEXT_DATA__ / AI-generated rules; the response body becomes `{ "data": { page_type, source, data } }` instead of HTML. Use `get_cookies=true` to receive JSON with the HTML, the cookies and `proxy`, the country of the exit that served the request.

parameters.name: url

schema.description: The page to fetch, a full `http(s)://` URL. URL-encode it when it has its own query string. Google search URLs answer 400: use `/serpApi`.
schema.title: Url

parameters.description: The page to fetch, a full `http(s)://` URL. URL-encode it when it has its own query string. Google search URLs answer 400: use `/serpApi`.

parameters.name: proxy_country

schema.description: Two-letter ISO country code (e.g. `de`, `us`) of the country the request is made from, so the site serves that country's prices, language and content. Omit it and the country is picked for you. An unsupported code answers 400 with the list of available countries.

parameters.description: Two-letter ISO country code (e.g. `de`, `us`) of the country the request is made from, so the site serves that country's prices, language and content. Omit it and the country is picked for you. An unsupported code answers 400 with the list of available countries.

parameters.name: markdown

schema.description: Return the page as clean Markdown (`text/markdown`) instead of HTML: headings, lists, tables, absolute links and images with alt text, without scripts, styles or markup. Built for LLMs, agents and RAG pipelines. Billed like an HTML call.

parameters.description: Return the page as clean Markdown (`text/markdown`) instead of HTML: headings, lists, tables, absolute links and images with alt text, without scripts, styles or markup. Built for LLMs, agents and RAG pipelines. Billed like an HTML call.

parameters.name: main_content_only

schema.description: With `markdown=true`: keep only the main content, without navigation, site header, footer and sidebars. Set to `false` for the whole page.
schema.title: Main Content Only

parameters.description: With `markdown=true`: keep only the main content, without navigation, site header, footer and sidebars. Set to `false` for the whole page.

parameters.name: get_cookies

schema.description: Return JSON with the page `html`, the `cookies` set during the visit and the `proxy` used, instead of HTML. Takes precedence over `parsed_data`.
schema.title: Get Cookies

parameters.description: Return JSON with the page `html`, the `cookies` set during the visit and the `proxy` used, instead of HTML. Takes precedence over `parsed_data`.

parameters.name: list_elements

schema.description: Return the page's interactive elements (buttons, inputs, selects, links, forms) with ready-to-use selectors instead of HTML, to help build `steps`.
schema.title: List Elements

parameters.description: Return the page's interactive elements (buttons, inputs, selects, links, forms) with ready-to-use selectors instead of HTML, to help build `steps`.

parameters.name: steps

schema.description: JSON array of browser actions to run after the page loads (wait_for, wait_for_text, wait, click, type, select, press_key, scroll). The request is rendered in a real browser and runs once.
schema.title: Steps

parameters.description: JSON array of browser actions to run after the page loads (wait_for, wait_for_text, wait, click, type, select, press_key, scroll). The request is rendered in a real browser and runs once.

200.description: Success — body is HTML (the target's own JSON as served when it answers with JSON; Markdown with `markdown=true`, JSON with `parsed_data=true` / `get_cookies=true`). With `parsed_data=true` a page that rendered but yielded no structured data is still a 200: `data.data` is empty, `data_extracted` is `false` and `html` carries the rendered page. Also a dead-origin 5xx page, as served (can be empty): then the `X-Origin-Status` header carries the target's status. The same for the target's own 401, 451 or empty 500, confirmed from more than one exit. A target that answers 204 (or another 2xx with no body) comes back as an empty 200. Billed.

400.description: Invalid URL, unsupported scheme or `proxy_country`, or `Hostname cannot be resolved` - the domain does not exist (billed).

404.description: The target itself answered 404 (the page does not exist). The body is the target's own page, as served (can be empty), and `X-Origin-Status: 404` tells it apart from a wrong API path. Billed - retrying returns the same answer.

410.description: The target itself answered 410 (the page is gone). Same shape as 404: the target's page with `X-Origin-Status: 410`. Billed.

403.description: Blocked by bot protection on every available bypass path.

415.description: The URL is not an HTML document (image, PDF, file); use /getImage for images. Not billed.

503.description: No render capacity on our side right now; not the target's fault, not billed - retry with backoff.

504.description: Request timed out: the call reached its time cap (60 s, 90 s with `steps`). Not billed.

523.description: Origin unreachable (target down or flapping, or our origin breaker is open); not a bot block, not billed - retry later.

post.summary: Scrape a Google search SERP for organic + ad results
post.description: Runs a Google web search for `keyword` and returns a normalized JSON structure with `topAds`, `bottomAds`, `organic` results, `totalResults`, `aiOverview` (Google's AI-written summary as `text` and `markdown`, the hostnames it cites as `sources`, and the cited pages as `references` with title, real URL, source, domain and snippet; `null` when the search has none), and the proxy country actually used. Set `pages_to_check` 1-10 to paginate. `wait_after_load` adds a delay after the SERP loads.

post.summary: Fetch an image in its original format
post.description: Downloads the image at `url` through rotating proxies and returns its bytes exactly as the image host serves them, with the host's own `Content-Type` (JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, GIF incl. animation, SVG, ICO, ...). Nothing is re-encoded. When the host answers with a bot challenge, a real browser opens the image and clears it. `url` must point at the image itself - for a page, use /getPageSource and take the image URL from its HTML.

parameters.name: url

schema.description: The image URL to fetch.
schema.title: Url

parameters.description: The image URL to fetch.

parameters.name: proxy_country

schema.description: Two-letter ISO country code (e.g. `de`, `us`) of the country the request is made from, so the site serves that country's prices, language and content. Omit it and the country is picked for you. An unsupported code answers 400 with the list of available countries.
schema.title: Proxy Country

parameters.description: Two-letter ISO country code (e.g. `de`, `us`) of the country the request is made from, so the site serves that country's prices, language and content. Omit it and the country is picked for you. An unsupported code answers 400 with the list of available countries.

200.description: The image bytes, unchanged, with the image's own `Content-Type`. `X-Destination-URL` carries the final URL after redirects. Billed.

400.description: Invalid URL, unsupported scheme or `proxy_country`, or `Hostname cannot be resolved` - the domain does not exist (billed).

403.description: Blocked by bot protection on every exit and in the browser, or the image host refused the URL itself (expired signed link; then `X-Origin-Status` is set). Not billed.

404.description: The image host answered 404 (the image does not exist); `X-Origin-Status: 404` tells it apart from a wrong API path. Billed.

410.description: The image host answered 410 (gone), with `X-Origin-Status: 410`. Billed.

413.description: The file is larger than 50 MB. Not billed.

415.description: The URL is not an image (an HTML page or another file type); `X-Resource-Content-Type` names what it is. Not billed.

504.description: Request timed out (75 s cap). Not billed.

523.description: Image host unreachable or answering 5xx on every exit (`X-Origin-Status` carries its status when it answered). Not a bot block, not billed - retry later.

post.description: Searches oopbuy.com for `keyword` and returns product listings as JSON: `title`, `titleCn`, `price` (in USD), `priceCny`, `monthSold`, `image`, `spu`, `channel`, and a product `url`. Pick the source marketplace with `channel` ('1688', 'taobao', or 'official'), order with `sort`, and page with `page`/`page_size`. Note: oopbuy trademark-blocks brand-name keywords at its own backend. That block is oopbuy's own genuine answer (it returns it as an HTTP 200 too), so we mirror it: brand queries come back as HTTP 200 with `keywordRejected: true` and an empty `results` array, not an error.

post.description:
Searches any regional eBay marketplace for `keyword` and returns the listings as JSON: `title`, `price` + `currency`, `condition` (with a normalised `conditionCode`), `seller` (username, feedback percentage and score), `shippingCost`, `sold`, `watchers`, `bids`, `image` and a clean item `url`. Filter with `condition`, `listing_type`, `min_price`/`max_price`, `free_shipping`, `seller` or `category`, sort with `sort`, and page with `page`/`page_size` (60, 120 or 240 per page). Set `marketplace` to search a specific site - prices, currency and availability differ between ebay.com, ebay.de, ebay.co.uk and the rest.

When eBay finds no exact match it still serves a full page of its own loosely-related suggestions. That case is reported honestly: `exactMatches` is `false` and a `notice` explains it, so those listings are never mistaken for real matches.

parameters.name: keyword

post.description:
Returns an Amazon ranked list for a category on any regional marketplace: Best Sellers (default), New Releases, Movers & Shakers, Most Wished For or Gift Ideas (`list_type`). The response carries the `category` (`name`, `slug`, `nodeId`, `url`, `parents`, `subcategories` - each with a url you can pass back as `category`) and up to `max_results` ranked `items`: `rank`, `asin`, `title`, `url`, `image`, `price` + `currency`, `offersCount`, `rating`, `reviewsCount`, and on Movers & Shakers `salesRank`, `previousSalesRank` and `salesRankChangePct`.

Pass `category` as a department slug (`electronics`), slug plus browse-node id (`electronics/172541`) or a pasted Amazon list url; leave it empty for the all-departments root (department list, no items). A list holds up to 100 items over two pages of 50, and each page fetched is billed as one request. When Amazon has no list for a category it says so, and that text is returned in `message` with an empty `items` array. An item whose card Amazon did not load (it loads ranks 31-50 of each page lazily) comes back with only `rank`, `asin` and `url`; `itemsWithDetails` counts the complete ones.

`proxy_country` defaults to the marketplace's home country (amazon.com -> US) so prices are in the store's currency.

Empty = the all-departments root, which returns the department list (`category.subcategories`) and no items.

post.summary: Scrape all reviews of an Airbnb listing
post.description: Given an Airbnb `room` (listing id or room URL), returns its guest `reviews`: `id`, `rating`, `text` (as written) with its `language`, `translatedText` (Airbnb's translation into `locale`), `date` (ISO), `localizedDate`, `stayDetail`, `photos`, `reviewer` (`id`, `name`, `photo`, `location` or `tenure`, `profileUrl`, `profileId`, `isSuperhost`, `deleted`) and the host's `response`. `reviewer.id` is Airbnb's account id (the one in its photo URLs; airbnb.com/users/show/<id> asks anonymous visitors to log in), while `profileUrl` is the public profile link Airbnb's own review cards open, keyed by a separate public id given as `profileId`. `deleted` is true when the guest has since closed their Airbnb account; Airbnb still sends the name, photo and location or tenure from the review, and they are returned as sent. Reads every review, not just the few on the room page: page with `page` (or `offset`) and `max_reviews` (up to 500 per call), order with `sort` (most_relevant, most_recent, highest_rated, lowest_rated) and drop older reviews with `since`. Also returns the `listing` summary (title, overall and category `rating`, `ratingDistribution`, `ratingCounts`, `reviewsCount`, `reviewTags`, host) and `totalResults`, `hasMore`, `nextPage`, `nextOffset`. `ratingDistribution` is Airbnb's own list of each star's share of the ratings as a 0-1 fraction (`{"stars": 5, "percentage": 0.957}` = 95.7%), not a count like the other review plugins return; `ratingCounts` gives the number of ratings per star (`{"5": 692, ...}`) worked out from those shares and `reviewsCount`, and is null when the shares do not fit it (seen on hotel listings, whose distribution covers more ratings than `reviewsCount`). Billed one unit per 50-review page read (`pagesFetched`). Companion to the Airbnb search (`/travel/airbnb`) and listing (`/travel/airbnb-room`) plugins.

post.description: Returns a company's Glassdoor employee reviews as JSON. Each review has `id`, `url`, `title`, `rating` (1-5), `subratings` (work/life balance, culture and values, diversity and inclusion, career opportunities, compensation and benefits, senior management), `recommendToFriend`, `ceoApproval`, `businessOutlook`, `pros`, `cons`, `advice`, `jobTitle`, `employmentStatus`, `isCurrentEmployee`, `yearsOfEmployment`, `location`, `date`, `helpfulCount`, `notHelpfulCount`, `featured`, `employerResponse` and `view` (the sort / filter view it came from). The response also carries `summary` (overall rating, review counts, recommend / CEO approval / business outlook percentages, the CEO, sub-rating averages, star distribution, reviews in the last 7 and 30 days), `companyMeta` (name, logo, website, industry, sector, headquarters, size) and `totalReviews`. The counts are Glassdoor's own and measure different sets: `totalReviews` is the number of reviews matching every filter of the call (`rating`, `job_title`, `keyword`, `topic`, `employment_status`, `language`, `current_only`; the default view is English reviews by full-time and part-time employees), the set the views read from. `summary.allReviewsCount` is every review Glassdoor holds for the employer, rated or not, in any language and employment status; no filter changes it. `summary.reviewCount` is the number of ratings behind `summary.overallRating`, and `summary.ratedReviewsCount` the number of reviews that carry a star rating; Glassdoor counts the two separately, so they can differ by a few. Both follow `rating` but not the language or employment filters, so they are usually above `totalReviews`. `summary.ratingDistribution` holds the star counts Glassdoor sends for its rating bars (`overall`, each sub-rating, and `recommendToFriend`); for employers with many reviews they cover only part of them (Google: 18,643 overall against a `reviewCount` of 52,845), so read them as proportions, not totals, and with `rating` set only that star is counted. `summary.reviewsLast7Days` and `reviewsLast30Days` count reviews matching the filters. Give `company` as a Glassdoor employer id, a Glassdoor company URL or a company name. Only US proxies are used (`proxy_country` accepts US or blank): Glassdoor redirects other countries to their local site, where these pages do not exist. post.summary: Scrape the reviews on an Amazon product page
post.description:
Returns the review data an Amazon product page shows to a signed-out visitor, as JSON: the overall `rating`, total `reviewCount` (global ratings), the 5..1-star `histogram` (percent per star), the AI `customersSay` summary (overall text plus per-aspect `sentiment`, `mentions`, `positive`, `negative`, `summary` and the quoted review `excerpts` Amazon shows for the aspect) and the top `reviews` (each with `id`, `url`, `author`, `rating`, `title`, `body`, `date`, `country`, `fromOtherCountry`, `verified`, `helpfulVotes`, `variant` and `images`). Identify the product with `asin` (plus `marketplace`) or a product `url`.

Scope: Amazon only shows its full review list to signed-in customers, so this endpoint returns the public slice on the product page - typically 5 to 13 top reviews, local ones first and then reviews from other countries - not a complete review export. When Amazon hides the top reviews behind a sign-in prompt (common on amazon.com), `reviewsGated` is `true` and `reviews` is empty; the rating, histogram and customers-say data, including its review excerpts, are still returned. Every field is always present and is `null` when the page does not show it. `proxy_country` defaults to the marketplace's home country; the country of the proxy that served the request is reported as `exitCountry`.

post.description: Given a Yelp `business` (page URL, alias or business id), returns the `business` summary (`businessId`, `alias`, `name`, `url`, `rating`, `reviewCount`, `ratingHistogram`, `reviewsCountByLanguage`, `categories`, `city`, `region`) and its `reviews`: `id`, `url`, `rating`, `text`, `language`, `publishedDate`, `date`, `user` (`name`, `location`, `reviewCount`, `friendCount`, `photoCount`, `isElite`, `eliteYear`), `photos`, `videos`, `reactions` (`helpful`, `thanks`, `loveThis`, `ohNo`), `ownerResponse`, `checkIns` and the author's `previousReviews`. Sort like yelp.com (`relevance`, `newest`, `oldest`, `highest`, `lowest`, `elites`), filter by `language`, star `rating`, a search `query` or `since` a date, and page with `page` / `start` up to `max_reviews` per call. To continue, call again with `start` = `nextStart` while `hasMore` is true: `nextStart` is the exact offset where this call stopped. `nextPage` is only set when that offset falls on a page boundary (a multiple of 10) and is null otherwise, because a page number would repeat reviews already returned. Counts: `business.reviewCount` is the review count Yelp shows for the business; `business.ratingHistogram` and `business.reviewsCountByLanguage` count the reviews in every language, and Yelp updates them separately from `reviewCount`, so their sums can differ from it by a few; `totalResults` is how many reviews match this call's `language`, `rating` and `query` (the total that `start` pages through). A business with no reviews returns an empty list; an unknown alias or URL is a 404. Billed one unit per 10 reviews returned (`pagesFetched`).

post.summary: Scrape one Etsy listing's full detail
post.description:
Fetches one Etsy listing (by `listing_id` or `url`) and returns it as JSON: `listingId`, `title`, `price` (the lowest price when variations differ, `priceMax` the highest), `originalPrice` / `onSale` / `discountPercent` / `saleEnds` during a sale, `currency` and `shopperRegion`, `availability` and `quantityAvailable`, `rating` and `reviewCount`, `reviewSummary` (item quality, shipping and service scores, recommend percentage, review tags and categories), the first `reviews`, `shop` (name, id, owner, location, rating, review count, sales, years on Etsy, Star Seller), `variations` (each menu with its options and their prices), `description`, `materials`, `highlights`, `category`, `shipping` (cost, origin, ships from, estimated delivery, processing time, returns), `images` and `video`.

Prices, shipping cost and VAT follow the shopper location Etsy assigns to the request, which can differ from `proxy_country`: `currency` and `shopperRegion` say which one a response used (e.g. EUR / BE), so read them before comparing prices. post.description: Returns Spotify catalog data as JSON, including the play counts and audience numbers the official Web API does not expose. `type=artist`: `artist` (`followers`, `monthlyListeners`, `worldRank`, `topCities`, `biography`, `externalLinks`, images, `verified`), `topTracks` with `playcount` (a top track's `album` carries `name` and `releaseDate` when Spotify lists that album among the artist's releases), `discography` groups (popular releases, albums, singles, compilations with totals), `relatedArtists`, `appearsOn`, `featuredOn` / `discoveredOn` playlists; `discography=true` adds the full `releases` list, paged. `type=album`: `album` (type, release date, label, copyright, artists, cover) and `tracks` with `playcount`, paged. `type=track`: `track` with `playcount`, duration, explicit flag, album and every credited artist. `type=playlist`: `playlist` (name, description, `followers`, owner, cover, `totalTracks`) and `tracks` with `playcount`, `addedAt`, `bpm` and `key`, paged. `type=search&query=`: `results` of `search_type` tracks, artists, albums or playlists, paged; a search with no match answers 200 with empty `results`. `playcount` comes only on artist, album, track and playlist lookups: Spotify's search does not return it, so search track results have no `playcount` key (look a track up with `type=track` for its count). `id` takes an open.spotify.com URL, a Spotify URI or a bare id. Lists page with `offset` / `max_results` and answer `hasMore` / `nextOffset`; each page fetched is one billed unit (`pagesFetched`).

post.description:
Returns the offers Amazon lists for a product under "All buying options", as JSON. Each offer has the seller (`sellerName`, `sellerId`, `sellerUrl`, `sellerRating`, `sellerRatingCount`, `sellerPositivePercent`), `price` + `currency`, `listPrice` and `savingsPercent`, `shippingPrice` and `totalPrice`, `condition` (as Amazon words it) with `conditionType` (new, used, collectible, refurbished) and the seller's `conditionNote`, `delivery` / `deliveryDate`, `alternativeDelivery` (the faster or Prime-member option Amazon also offers), `shipsFrom`, `soldByAmazon`, `fulfilledByAmazon`, `prime`, the `offerId` and a `buyBoxWinner` flag. The response also carries the product `title`, `rating`, `reviewCount`, `image` and `totalOffers`.

Page 1 starts with the Buy Box (featured) offer, also returned as `buyBox`; Amazon shows it whatever filter is set. Amazon lists 10 other offers per page: follow `nextPage`, or read up to 5 pages in one call with `pages`. Filter with `condition`, `free_shipping` and `prime`. `shippingPrice` is 0 for free delivery and null when Amazon shows no delivery promise for the location. `proxy_country` defaults to the marketplace's home country so prices and delivery are the ones a local shopper sees; the country of the proxy that served the request is reported as `exitCountry`.

post.description: Searches a Shopee market (Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines, Taiwan or Brazil - `country`) for `q` and returns one page of results: up to 40 `products`, each with `position`, `itemId`, `shopId`, `name`, `url`, `image`, `price`, `originalPrice` (when Shopee shows the crossed-out price), `discountPercent`, `isPixPrice`, `currency`, `rating` (average stars), `location` (where the seller ships from) and `labels` (promotion badges). `sort` orders the results, `min_price` / `max_price` filter them, `shop_id` keeps one shop's products (or lists the shop without `q`), and `url` takes a Shopee search or category link instead. Shopee shows one page per search, so run several sort orders or price ranges for more products. `price` is what Shopee shows a signed-out shopper, which can be a promotional or new-customer price (see `labels`). In Brazil a card often shows the Pix price (`isPixPrice: true`): `price` is then the Pix price and `discountPercent` is measured against the list price, which Shopee does not show on such a card, so `originalPrice` is null. post.description: Searches publix.com (US) for `query` at one store and returns `products`: `productId`, `itemCode`, `title`, `brand`, `size`, `url`, `image`, `price`, `priceText`, `unit` (e.g. 'lb' for items sold by weight), `wasPrice`, `currency`, `onSale`, `promotion` (`type` such as BOGO, `message`, `conditions`, `validThrough`, `savings`), `hasCoupon`, `soldByWeight`, `aisle`, `category`, `categoryPath` and `storeId`, plus `store` (the store the prices are for), `totalResults`, `totalPages` and `nextPage`. Publix publishes a price online only while an item is on promotion, so `price` is null for the rest. A keyword Publix sends to a category returns that category, named in `redirectedTo`; one it sends to a page that lists no products (the weekly ad, cake ordering, store locations) answers with no products and `sentElsewhere` true.
